note: Review of bcdaca6: approvals carry through clear and handoff-resume links (owner 2026-10-23 xxxxxxxx-27 revised), but nothing wrote a handoff-resume link. `pin --resumed-from` now writes it, fail closed, for a fresh session (records startup/resume only, no link yet) resuming the newest handoff of an ended predecessor that has no /clear successor, after claiming the predecessor by exclusive create. Checked: a fresh session resuming its predecessor's published handoff carries the checked approval (pin and measure print it; HEAD is still the target's commit), locate then reads it as successor, and the session's own next handoff publishes with the carried id; a fork and a background copy (no lineage file, started as fork) pin the same file and carry nothing, and both are refused at publish; a second fresh session finds the predecessor claimed; a live predecessor, an older handoff, a /clear-ended predecessor and a session with no record are never linked. Root reading 2026-10-23 (fail closed, the owner to confirm): when P is resumed after S claimed it, P's handoff dated before the claim is context only for approvals on P's line (P and its /clear successor), while S and S's /clear successor still carry it; a handoff P writes after the claim is P's own and carries on P's line only, not on S's (slice A review: S and S's /clear successor read it as `written after the claim`; S repeating its line is refused). The resumed P's quote checks count only rows after the claim (owner 21:47 "1. OK"), so P repeating its pre-claim line is refused at publish and a compaction summary's copy lists it unchecked. The claim is checked for every session from the reader up to the writer, so a handoff of P's /clear predecessor P0 dated before the claim carries on S's line and not on P's.
